inputs.text: [happily] Listen! Today [excited] we're going all the way back to the very beginning. Before there was even an Earth.
[curious] Before the Earth? Then what was there?
[playful][calm] A cloud. A giant cloud of dust and gas, spinning around the Sun, [softly] which was brand new too.
[amazed] A cloud… can a cloud turn into a planet?
[warmly] It sure can. Little by little, all those grains of dust stuck together. [serious] That was gravity: an invisible force [calm] that pulls everything toward the middle.
[excited] The ball grew, and grew, and grew. [pauses] And deep down, the heaviest metals sank to the bottom. They made the core, [amazed] the Earth's burning-hot heart.
[curious] Does that time have a name?
[serious][calm] It's called the Hadean. [softly] The name comes from Hades, the Greek god of the underworld, [calm] because the Earth looked like an underworld made of lava.
[gasps] Was there any water yet, at least?
[sad] Not yet. It was much too hot for that. [softly] Volcanoes everywhere, and lava as far as you could see.
[calm] But little by little, the Earth cooled down. [pauses] Slowly, over millions of years.
[happily][excited] And then it started to rain! [gasps] A giant rain, falling for a very, very long time, filled up the low places on the Earth.
[warmly] That's how the very first oceans were born. [pauses] And in that water, [amazed] the greatest adventure was about to begin.
